question: Do the reduced high-frequency auxiliary modes lift to homogeneous full tensor Hessian modes on the retained off-shell seed?

primary_sources.title: Anderson, Molina-Paris and Mottola, Cosmological Horizon Modes and Linear Response in de Sitter Spacetime
primary_sources.locator: Section I, equations (2)-(3) and the following description of linear response around a self-consistent background; section III, (28)-(29)
primary_sources.use: Established distinction between causal metric response, local contacts and independent state variations, formulated around a self-consistent background. The paper does not establish the charged seed obstruction and its elimination of Planck-scale branches is not adopted.

comparison: The preceding theorem proves reduced auxiliary resonances while leaving the full constraints open. Earlier local Ward identities show why two rows alone are insufficient. This argument retains the residual in the full logarithmic chart, proves a nonzero outer trace collar from the magnetic anomaly, and combines a differentiated metric trace with simple-zero gluing to exclude any nontrivial full homogeneous Hessian kernel in the specified high-frequency auxiliary sector.
hardest_steps: Identify the exact full chart-density tensor response off shell rather than replacing it with the raw equation derivative.
Upgrade both shape and reconstructed conformal tails to C1 endpoint estimates using the two retained scalar graph bounds.
Glue the proportionality constants across all simple fast zeros without assuming an asymptotic expansion or analyticity for the unknown orbit residual.
next_decision: Use the reduced resonances only as auxiliary diagnostics. Resolve the signed nonlinear compatibility and construct a self-consistent geometry, or establish a controlled transfer of the full constrained response to one; the residual obstruction vanishes on shell and does not establish physical mode exclusion or stability.
